en: Paccuppannānāgatavāra (The Chapter on the Present and the Future)
He who fully understands the aggregate of form will also fully understand the aggregate of feeling? No.
Or rather, he who will fully understand the aggregate of feeling has already fully understood the aggregate of form? No.
He who does not fully understand the aggregate of form will also not fully understand the aggregate of feeling?
Those who will attain the path do not fully understand the aggregate of form, yet they will not fail to fully understand the aggregate of feeling.
However, the arahants and those worldlings who will not attain the path do not fully understand the aggregate of form and will also not fully understand the aggregate of feeling.
Or again, is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the aggregate of feeling will also not fully understand the aggregate of form?
One who possesses the supreme path (aggamagga-samaṅgī) will not fully understand the aggregate of feeling, yet he does not fail to fully understand the aggregate of form.
An Arahant and those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path will neither fully understand the aggregate of feeling nor [fully understand] the aggregate of form.
And they do not fully understand the aggregate of form.
